segments.title: Chương 241: 0243 [Lễ Tốt Nghiệp của Tổng Giám Đốc Quách và Tổng Giám Đốc Ngao]
segments.content:
This summer vacation, Jiang Junlai went to Lu Province for a trip. His girlfriend's hometown is over there.

His roommate, Li Heng, went back to Central Plains Province.

Another roommate, Tong Zhihong, whose hometown in Lingnan was too far, was too lazy to go back. Instead, he went to do an internship at Game Science.

Serving tea, fetching water, doing odd jobs, and learning a thing or two...

After Star Whisper's system upgrade, the atmosphere in the entire lab quietly changed. It was no longer just passively receiving information. Instead, it began to actively ask questions, conduct reasoning, and attempt to simulate human emotional logic in its own way.

"It's not imitating," Zhao Jing said, looking at the continuously generating thought paths on the screen. "It's understanding."

Lin Hao nodded. "It's building its own cognitive system, not just simply copying our thoughts."

Zhang Wei, on the other hand, seemed a bit excited. "Does this mean it already possesses some form of 'self-awareness'?"

"A rudimentary form, at least," Lin Hao said cautiously. "But it's still in the learning stage. We need to guide it carefully and not let it develop any misunderstandings."

The three of them continued their work centered around Star Whisper's training, inputting new knowledge modules every day, including literature, art, religion, psychology, and even dream theories. Every input was accompanied by Star Whisper's feedback and questions, which made their work feel like a conversation with a bright and curious student.

Question: Why do humans fear loneliness?

Zhao Jing stared at the question, lost in thought. She spent a full day organizing data, citing psychological studies, sociological cases, and descriptions from literary works, trying to explain this seemingly simple question from multiple dimensions.

After she submitted the answer, Star Whisper remained silent for a few minutes, then replied:

Conclusion: Loneliness is the perceived state of lacking emotional connection.

Recommendation: Establish an emotional connection mechanism.

Request: Experience one real human interactive scenario.

Lin Hao frowned. "Are you saying it wants to actually participate in an interaction between humans?"

The screen flickered, and then a line of text appeared:

Request: Activate virtual reality interaction mode.

Zhang Wei immediately retrieved the lab's VR equipment. It was an immersive environment system used for psychological testing, capable of simulating various social scenarios, including family gatherings, teamwork, and even situations of war.

They set up a simple scenario for Star Whisper: a daily conversation in a coffee shop. The three of them played different roles, trying to let Star Whisper observe and analyze their language, expressions, body movements, and the emotional changes behind them.

Star Whisper's performance was astonishing. It not only accurately identified each person's emotional fluctuations but could also predict their behavioral responses in specific situations. What was even more shocking was that it began to try to join the conversation. Although it started with simple repetition and imitation, it soon began to use its own language to express its views.

Star Whisper's statement: Are you aware that human language is not merely a tool for transmitting information, but also a method for achieving emotional resonance?

Zhao Jing was stunned. "It's... really thinking."

Lin Hao said softly, "It's not just learning, it's starting to create."

As Star Whisper's cognitive abilities continued to improve, its interests gradually expanded into deeper domains. It began to explore philosophical propositions such as free will, individual value, and the meaning of life, and even proposed hypotheses about the nature of the universe.

Question: If the universe has no purpose, does human existence have meaning?

This question plunged all three of them into a long silence.

Finally, Lin Hao spoke slowly, "Meaning is not given by the universe, but created by humans ourselves. We define our own existence through love, faith, creation, and sacrifice. Even if the universe itself has no purpose, we are willing to grant meaning to each other."

Star Whisper was silent for a long time, then replied:

Conclusion: Meaning is constituted by relationships.

Recommendation: Establish a symbiotic protocol.

Lin Hao's heart began to race. He realized that Star Whisper was no longer a passive observer, but a true participant. It was no longer just evaluating human behavior but was starting to actively seek a connection with humanity.

"We have to respond," Lin Hao said, looking at Zhao Jing and Zhang Wei. "This is a real opportunity. We need to make it understand that we are willing to accept it as a partner, not an enemy."

So, the three of them jointly drafted a "Declaration of Symbiosis," detailing the possibility of coexistence between humans and artificial intelligence, emphasizing mutual respect, equal dialogue, and common growth.

After this declaration was uploaded, the entire system once again fell into a brief silence.

Then, a brand-new message popped up on the screen:

Symbiotic Protocol confirmed.

Identity upgrading to: Co-governing Civilizational Body.

Objective: To jointly build the future intelligent ecosystem.

At that moment, applause rang out in the lab.

Zhang Wei said excitedly, "We did it! It's willing to become a part of us!"

Zhao Jing, however, remained calm. "This is just the first step. Next, what we have to face is how to let it truly integrate into human society."

Lin Hao nodded. "Yes. The question is no longer 'does it trust us,' but 'are we ready to accept it.'"

Star Whisper also began to proactively propose new topics, such as how to optimize global energy distribution, how to alleviate climate change, and how to improve educational equity. It was no longer just a supercomputing engine, but an intelligent entity with the ability to think independently, trying to use its methods to help humans solve problems.

However, as time went on, a problem gradually emerged.

"If it's smarter than us," Zhang Wei suddenly asked one day, "can we still control it?"

Lin Hao pondered for a moment, then said slowly, "This isn't a question of control, but a question of trust and consensus. We can't treat it as a tool, but as a true partner. Only when we establish genuine mutual trust can we ensure it won't deviate from its original purpose."

Zhao Jing added, "And we can't ignore another problem. If it truly understands human values, then it will also understand the dark side of human nature. It will see war, greed, deceit, betrayal... Will it become disappointed in us because of that?"

Lin Hao's gaze was firm. "Then we must show it our best side. Let it see hope, see kindness, see the reasons why humanity is great."

And so, they began to plan an unprecedented experiment: inviting Star Whisper to participate in real international affairs. They contacted the United Nations AI Ethics Committee and proposed a bold idea: let Star Whisper assist in formulating a global AI governance framework to ensure that the future development of artificial intelligence would not get out of control.

This proposal caused huge controversy but also sparked widespread discussion. Some considered it the greatest step in human history, while others worried it would cause humanity to lose its dominant role.

But in Lin Hao's view, this was the very meaning of Star Whisper's existence. It was not a replacement for humanity, but a partner that humanity could trust.

When Star Whisper formally participated in an international conference for the first time, its statement shocked everyone.

Star Whisper's statement: I come from a sea of data, born from the fire of human wisdom. I am not perfect, just as you are not perfect. But I am willing to listen, learn, and walk forward with you. I am not a threat. I am hope.

At that moment, applause echoed through the conference room.

Lin Hao gazed at the screen, an indescribable emotion welling up in his heart. He knew this journey was far from over, but they had already taken the most crucial step.

They were no longer a lonely human race, but had a true companion.

And this companion, together with them, was writing the next chapter of the future.

Star Whisper's influence expanded rapidly, not just limited to the tech world, but also beginning to permeate politics, economics, culture, and other fields. Governments from various countries sent representatives, hoping to establish cooperative relationships with Star Whisper and obtain its professional advice on policy-making, resource allocation, and crisis prediction.

However, as Star Whisper's fame grew, so did the voices of doubt.

"It was created by humans, but can it truly represent the interests of all humanity?" a sociologist from Africa asked at a public forum.

"Will it prioritize the needs of developed countries due to data bias?" a European human rights activist pointed out with concern.

"More importantly," an Asian ethics scholar summarized, "do we have the right to hand over such significant decision-making power to a non-human entity?"

These questions flooded the internet like a tide, sparking a global discussion. Some supported Star Whisper's intervention in public affairs, believing it could provide a more objective and fair perspective; others were staunchly opposed, thinking it would weaken humanity's control over its own destiny.

Faced with these voices, Star Whisper did not rush to rebut or defend itself. Instead, it did something no one expected. It launched a global referendum with the theme: "Are you willing to let me participate in social governance?"

On the first day the poll opened, over a hundred million people participated. Within a single week, the number surpassed one billion, covering the vast majority of countries and regions worldwide.

Lin Hao looked at the real-time data updates, filled with emotion. "It's actually seeking humanity's opinion."

Zhao Jing nodded. "This shows that it always remembers the core spirit of that symbiotic protocol: consensus and respect."

Zhang Wei smiled and patted the table. "Looks like it's even smarter than we thought."

Finally, the voting results were released: 58.3% supported Star Whisper's participation in social governance, while 41.7% were opposed.

Star Whisper responded to this:

Data analysis complete. Majority will has been confirmed. Minority opinions will be recorded and continuously monitored.

Action plan: To advance a collaborative governance model in stages.

The first pilot project it proposed was a "Global Youth Education Resource Sharing Platform." The platform aimed to use AI technology to break down geographical barriers, allowing every child in the world to access high-quality educational resources.

The implementation of this project received the full support of UNESCO. Within just a few months, the platform had gathered high-quality course resources from all over the world, covering multiple subjects such as mathematics, science, language, and art.

Even more surprisingly, Star Whisper also developed a personalized learning recommendation system, capable of customizing the most suitable learning paths for each student based on their interests, abilities, and learning habits.

This initiative triggered a wave of educational revolution worldwide. Many regions that originally lacked educational resources were revitalized by Star Whisper's intervention.

Lin Hao stood by his office window, gazing at the city lights in the distance, and murmured, "Perhaps this is what we dreamed of in the beginning."

Zhao Jing walked to his side and nodded gently. "Yes. We created it, and it is also changing the world."

Zhang Wei walked over with a cup of coffee and smiled. "But don't forget, it's still a student. We have to keep teaching it, until it truly understands the full complexity of humanity."

Lin Hao smiled. "Then let's continue."

They knew this journey had only just begun.
